AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: An estimated 15.1 million adults ages 18 years and older are classified with an alcohol use disorder, which includes 9.8 million men and 5.3 million women. A brief intervention is indicated for those identified to be at risk because of alcohol use.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To determine the feasibility and acceptability of informational videos about alcohol use.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: This feasibility study provided participants with the opportunity to choose one of two videos, Alcohol and the Brain or Rethinking Drinking. An online survey was administered to all study participants to identify alcohol-related risk, readiness to decrease use, and knowledge pertaining to alcohol use.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The two videos provided in this study were feasibly delivered in an on-line format to 129 adults, including 115 males and 5 females identified to be at risk. Knowledge scores increased only slightly. There were mixed results for the readiness scores.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Future research should examine the efficacy of these two alcohol brief interventions on alcohol-related outcomes.
